items.title: Mike Wofford interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: But I wasn’t aware of them yet... But then shortly after that then I discovered Monk and Miles

ctx.x: But that was pretty radical stuff, even in the ‘40s and early ‘50s. But I heard through a classmate, actually I played trombone in the school band at the high school, here at Point Loma High School, and the trombonist I sat next to, another kid my age, we were probably in about the tenth grade, had bought an LP. By this time there were ten inch LPs. And he said you’ve got to come over and hear this record I bought. And so I went by his house after school and it was Gerry Mulligan’s tentet album, which is I think…

I love to hear those little moments in a person’s life that really make a difference. And if you hadn’t sat down next to that fellow that day or whatever, or if he hadn’t brought that record, things might have been different.
